title: Environment access & evidence playbook
summary: Practical playbook mapping roles, minimal policy snippets, audit-log field guidance, SIEM export best practices, and an automated evidence bundle workflow tailored per environment (hosted, dedicated, private). Designed as a working reference for RBAC v2 rollout and audit automation engineers.
iam_matrix:
Principals and recommended default capabilities (short):
- human-admin: account-level management, billing-read, user-management; in hosted limited via org-scope; in dedicated mapped to customer-admin; in private mapped from customer IdP.
- human-dev: non-prod deploys, logs-read; deny prod-rollout in hosted; prod access only via canary elevation.
- svc-infra: cluster lifecycle (scale, allocate), autoscale hooks; explicit KMS decrypt only in dedicated with condition.
- svc-customer: only present in dedicated or private deployments; never in hosted.
- runtime: ephemeral token with scoped model-artifact:get, kvcache:read, metrics:write; TTL <= 15m, must use mTLS.
Matrix notes: enforce permission boundaries and deny-by-default statements in hosted roles to prevent accidental cross-tenant data access.
policy_snippets:
Small, copyable least-privilege examples (replace {{PLACEHOLDERS}}):
1) Hosted "org-dev-lite":
Version: 2025-01-01; Statements: Allow [console:view, models:list, jobs:create:dev] on arn:redwood:org:{{ORG_ID}}:project/*; Deny [jobs:create:prod, billing:*] on *; Notes: attach MFA requirement for sensitive actions.
2) Dedicated infra-runner:
Version: 2025-01-01; Statements: Allow [compute:allocate_gpu, clusters:scale, models:serve:create] on arn:redwood:dedicated:{{CUSTOMER_ID}}:pool/{{POOL_ID}}; Allow kms:decrypt on arn:cloudkms:{{REGION}}:key/{{KEY_ID}} with condition aws:SecureTransport=true.
3) Private local-ops template:
Granted via IdP group mapping. Permissions: node lifecycle, artifact push to internal repo, read-only data access by default. Hardware secrets accessible only via HSM-wrapped keys.
4) Short-lived grant (canary) pattern:
- Issue canary token tied to PR number and approval id; TTL <= 1 hour; log issuance event with evidence_ref and approval_ticket in manifest.
environment_guidance:
Operational rules and differences (practical):
Hosted: multi-tenant control plane, no hosted role should read raw tenant data; use enforcement denials and JIT approvals for any elevated data access. Network egress and per-tenant KMS keys required.
Dedicated: customer principals can be onboarded to customer-owned pools; infra roles manage capacity but do not get tenant PII by default. Billing telemetry is centrally aggregated and access controlled.
Private: customer-managed control plane recommended; Redwood provides role templates and mapping guidance. All sensitive operations gated by local approval flows and HSM/KMS usage; automation requires explicit customer consent for dataset mounts.
Delegation patterns: canary short-lived grants with audit hooks; break-glass role with timebox, mandatory postmortem and automated SIEM evidence marker.
audit_log_schema:
Canonical fields for exported audit events (NDJSON preferred):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (UUID)
- principal_type (human, service, runtime)
- principal_id (user:alice@redwood.com or svc:infra-42)
- principal_roles (comma-separated role names)
- action (canonical: jobs.create, models.download, kms.decrypt)
- resource (arn-like resource string)
- outcome (success, failure, denied, throttled)
- request_id (ingress correlation id)
- src_ip, user_agent, region (flattened context)
- policy_rule (id of rule that allowed/denied)
- before_snapshot, after_snapshot (short text diffs, max 4096 chars)
- evidence_refs (comma-separated artifact ids)
Notes: keep field names stable across environments; include request_id and event_id for cross-correlation with SIEM and evidence bundles.
siem_export:
Best practices and detection guidance:
- Format: NDJSON; include event_id and request_id for linking.
- Do not sample authorization denials or break-glass/canary events. Non-sensitive telemetry may be sampled (log sampling metadata required).
- Enrichment: attach customer_id when applicable, escalate kms.decrypt and data.export as high-risk event types.
- Key detections to implement: repeated denies to sensitive resources, elevation without approval ticket, long-lived runtime tokens, unusual KMS decrypt patterns.
- Retention guidance: hot logs 90 days, indexed summaries 1 year, archived cold storage 7 years for regulated customers.
- Integrations: Splunk, Elastic, Chronicle connectors recommended; include a stable mapping layer to reuse detection rules.
evidence_automation:
Automated evidence collection flow (working):
1) Triggers: role grants, canary issuance, break-glass activation, policy changes, kms key use, model artifact publish.
2) Artifact set: filtered audit NDJSON (48h for principal), role-binding snapshot, active tokens snapshot for principal, approval ticket/PR references, config diffs.
3) Bundle: tar.gz with manifest.txt (flat text), hashes, and an evidence_id; upload to secure immutable bucket.
4) SIEM marker: emit evidence.created event with evidence_id for correlation.
5) Access controls: compliance roles and requestor read access for 30 days, then archival read-only.
Implementation notes: event-driven serverless workers preferred; all fetches logged and signed; any evidence containing customer data requires an approval token recorded in manifest.
operational_notes:
Implementation and rollout considerations:
- Use permission boundaries to limit what customer-mapped admin roles can do to Redwood control plane.
- Implement a decryption proxy for hosted per-tenant decrypts if direct kms:decrypt is undesirable.
- Canary issuance must log approval_ticket and evidence_ref atomically to avoid gaps.
- Provide a lightweight CLI to snapshot RBAC bindings for auditors (rbac-snapshot).
- Test evidence bundle generation in private/offline environments using a mocked signer and upload path.
- Define SLA target for evidence bundles on break-glass: 1 hour; assess feasibility for air-gapped private deployments.
